hero.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named FSL Pitcher of the Week
hero.teaser: The 22-year-old left-hander struck out 12 batters over seven scoreless innings in two appearances against Fort Myers.
hero.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for July 20-26, Minor League Baseball announced Monday.

Ware made two appearances against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels at Clover Park, starting Tuesday and returning for a relief outing Sunday. The left-hander combined to throw seven scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two walks while striking out 12 batters.

The Mets won both games in which Ware appeared. He earned the victory Sunday after pitching four scoreless innings, allowing one hit and one walk and recording a career-high eight strikeouts as St. Lucie rallied for an 11-8 win.

Ware, 22, was selected by the New York Mets in the 15th round of the 2025 MLB Draft out of LSU. He made his professional debut with St. Lucie in April and has remained with the team throughout the season.

cards.headline: Judge rules James Fishback can remain on Florida governor ballot after residency challenge
cards.body:
Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback will remain on Florida's Aug. 18 primary ballot after Leon County Circuit Judge David Frank rejected Lt. Gov. Jay Collins' challenge to his residency qualifications. Frank ruled Monday that Collins did not present enough evidence to overcome Florida's legal presumptions favoring continued residency and candidate access to the ballot. The judge wrote that the court will not be deciding the race between the lieutenant governor and Fishback, adding that decision will be in the sound hands of the voters. The final order denies Collins' request to remove Fishback, declares that the Department of State properly certified his candidacy and says Fishback shall remain qualified for the Republican nomination for governor.

Collins sued Fishback in June, arguing the candidate failed to meet the Florida Constitution's requirement that a governor reside in the state for the seven years preceding the election. During an expedited hearing last week, Collins' attorneys presented voter registration, mortgage, tax and homestead records they argued showed Fishback established legal residency in Washington, D.C., between 2019 and 2022. Fishback voted in Washington during the 2020 presidential election, filed D.C. resident income tax returns and signed mortgage paperwork describing a condominium there as his principal residence. Property tax records also showed the condominium received a D.C. homestead deduction. A forensic document examiner testified it was probable Fishback signed the disputed voter registration form.

Frank acknowledged those records could carry consequences outside the Florida candidacy case, writing that it may be true the various election and financial filings could result in regulatory, maybe even more severe legal, repercussions for Fishback under Washington, D.C. law. But the judge found they did not prove Fishback intended to abandon Florida as his permanent home. Fishback testified for several hours that he never intended to move his legal domicile from Florida. He acknowledged signing mortgage paperwork identifying the Washington condominium as his primary residence but said he rushed through the documents without reading them closely. He also characterized his 2020 D.C. vote as an inadvertent registration during the pandemic, saying he was staying with his parents and wanted to vote for President Donald Trump. Frank found Fishback credible on the central issue of intent, stating that despite defendant stating at various points his residence was in Washington, D.C., defendant never had an actual subjective intent to move his permanent residency from Florida.

Fishback's campaign called the ruling a victory for the Constitution and for every Floridian who believes elections should be decided by voters. Collins' attorney Mark Meuser criticized the ruling and argued the court improperly accepted Fishback's explanation that he did not understand the legal significance of his Washington filings. Meuser did not indicate whether Collins plans to appeal the ruling. Unless an appellate court intervenes, Fishback will remain on the Aug. 18 Republican primary ballot alongside Collins, U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and former House Speaker Paul Renner.

cards.headline: Florida families say Medicaid abruptly stopped covering autism therapy without explanation
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County parents say their children lost access to Applied Behavioral Analysis after Medicaid stopped covering the therapy. Florida's health agency has not explained why.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County parents say their children lost access to Applied Behavioral Analysis after Medicaid abruptly stopped covering it. The Cleveland Clinic describes ABA as a research based behavior therapy for people with autism and other developmental disorders, adding that many studies have proven the effectiveness of ABA. Families connected to Reflection Services ABA Therapy in Lake Worth say they received notice that Medicaid would no longer cover their children's treatment. Daura Mabel Sanchez Cano de Fundora said her son David is classified by his neurologist as level one on the autism spectrum. She described how his vocabulary has been increasingly amazing and he can understand what is happening. Myrian Suarez, a mother of two boys with autism, said ABA gave her son tools to manage his emotions.

Since the therapy stopped, families described dangerous regressions in their children's behavior. Talia Quiroz said she has bites all over her body. Suarez described bruised arms from her son's pinching. Melissa Moran, a registered behavior technician at Reflection Services ABA Therapy, acknowledged the cost of the services but warned of societal repercussions. She said parents may not go to work, affecting the economy, and that some kids have unsafe behaviors including physical aggression and self injurious behaviors that may put themselves and other kids at risk.

Reports of Medicaid cuts to ABA therapy have surfaced in states across the country. The Health and Human Services Office of the Inspector General audited Medicaid spending on ABA in Maine, Michigan, Wisconsin and Colorado, identifying roughly $197.9 million in what it considers improper payments among the four states. A separate audit in Nebraska found yearly Medicaid spending on ABA therapy multiplied 18 times over across a five year period. U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. said during a news conference last week that the administration is not sending Medicaid and Medicare dollars out the door until it has confidence they are being spent lawfully and appropriately.

cards.headline: Armed robbery at Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce forces victim to withdraw cash
cards.teaser: A man using a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce was forced to withdraw cash at gunpoint Sunday night after two men approached him, one displaying a concealed firearm.
cards.body:
The Fort Pierce Police Department said the robbery happened Sunday at about 8:38 p.m. when two men approached the victim at the Wells Fargo ATM. One of the men displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw an unknown amount of cash. The two suspects then fled the scene on foot.

Officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department responded to the scene, established a perimeter and used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects. The suspects were not located. Police described the suspects as two men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie bans gas station at Tradition development site after months of resident concerns
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council unanimously approved a permanent ban on gas stations at a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive. The council voted July 13 to finalize the 16th amendment to the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development, ending nearly three months of debate that began when Winding River Crosstown LLC requested permission to convert the site from residential to commercial use.

The amendment changes the parcel designation from residential to commercial while permanently prohibiting any current or future owner from developing a service station on the property. The restriction was added after Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo and other council members raised concerns during a May 26 hearing that a convenience store with gas pumps would worsen traffic along Crosstown Parkway west of Interstate 95. The council initially tabled the request to allow staff time to review whether gas stations could be eliminated as a permitted use.

Several Heritage Oaks residents urged the council during a June 22 hearing to reject the land-use change, citing concerns about increased traffic, noise and neighborhood impacts. The developer agreed to permanently relinquish the right to build a gas station, and the council voted 4-0 to approve the commercial designation on first reading. City planner Bridget Kean said the restriction is now written directly into the Tradition MPUD documents, ensuring no future owner can develop a gas station on the parcel.

Councilman Anthony Bonna defended the decision at the July 13 meeting, saying expanding commercial development will benefit residents by broadening the city's tax base. Bonna said Port St. Lucie has long lacked commercial development, which places a burden on homeowners. Before any mass grading begins, the developer must install a fence along the southern property line to prevent construction access through Southwest Glenbrook Drive. An architectural wall and landscape buffering must be completed along the southeastern and southern boundaries before the first building permit is issued for vertical construction.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds challenges David Jolly to Florida governor debates before primary concludes
cards.teaser: Republican front runner Byron Donalds challenged leading Democratic candidate David Jolly to three general election debates this fall, even as Donalds continues facing three opponents for the GOP nomination.
cards.body:
Republican gubernatorial front runner Byron Donalds challenged leading Democratic candidate David Jolly to three general election debates this fall with less than a month remaining before Florida's Aug. 18 primary. Donalds continues facing three opponents for the GOP nomination. Donalds said when the time comes for these debates, his vision is one for a free Florida that puts the people of Florida first, protects the Florida dream, expands Florida's economies and makes sure Florida remains number one in all of America. Jolly, a former Republican congressman now running as a Democrat, initially responded by telling Donalds to survive his own primary first. During a later CNN appearance, however, he said he would gladly meet Donalds on the debate stage a dozen times, adding that Donalds should get through his Republican primary first.

The exchange gave Donalds' Republican opponents another opportunity to criticize the front runner for looking beyond them. Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner and businessman James Fishback have not received debate invitations from Donalds. Donalds has not debated his primary rivals while maintaining sizable advantages in polling, fundraising and endorsements. A recent Cygnal survey showed Donalds at 43 percent, compared with 12 percent for Fishback, 11 percent for Collins and 2 percent for Renner, although nearly one third of voters remained undecided.

A separate University of North Florida poll offered an early look at the possible general election matchup. Donalds led Jolly 46 percent to 41 percent among likely midterm voters, with a margin of error of 3.8 percentage points. The poll surveyed 848 likely midterm voters from July 8 through July 17.

cards.headline: Poll shows Florida property tax amendment support drops after voters learn of budget impact
cards.teaser: A University of North Florida poll found 61 percent initial support for Florida's proposed property tax amendment. Support fell to 45 percent after respondents were told the proposal is estimated to create an approximately $11.8 billion municipal budget shortfall over two years.
cards.body:
A new poll showed Florida's proposed property tax amendment may be popular enough to pass depending on how it is described to voters. The proposal would raise the homestead exemption for non school property taxes from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and then to $250,000 in 2028. It would also lower the annual assessment growth cap for non homestead properties from 10 percent to 5 percent and restrict how local governments spend remaining property tax revenue. The University of North Florida survey initially found 61 percent support after respondents were told the amendment would reserve property tax revenue for core public services. That is narrowly above the 60 percent approval required for a constitutional amendment.

Support fell 16 points after respondents were told the proposal is estimated to create an approximately $11.8 billion municipal budget shortfall over two years. With that information, 45 percent supported the amendment and 47 percent opposed it. The poll surveyed 848 likely midterm voters from July 8 through July 17. Those results add significance to three lawsuits challenging the amendment's ballot title and summary. Plaintiffs argue phrases promising to protect small businesses, ensure fairness and preserve core services amount to political advertising instead of a neutral description of the proposal.

The challengers are not asking a judge to remove the amendment from the November ballot. If the language is found defective, state law would require Attorney General James Uthmeier to rewrite what voters see. A hearing on the ballot language challenges is scheduled for July 29 in Leon County. The cases could be consolidated ahead of that hearing.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County commissioners deadlock on infrastructure sales tax referendum timing
hero.body:
St. Lucie County commissioners split 2-2 on July 21 over whether to ask voters in November 2026 or November 2028 to renew the county's half-cent infrastructure sales tax, which expires in December 2028 after its 10-year authorization. With Vice Chairman Larry Leet absent, the board voted unanimously to postpone the decision until its Aug. 4 meeting, when Leet is expected to return and cast the deciding vote.

Three Port St. Lucie officials urged commissioners to place the referendum on the 2026 ballot before the vote. Public Works Director Colt Schwerdt said the tax has funded road, sidewalk, stormwater and water-quality improvements that have benefited city residents. Utility Systems Director Kevin Matyjaszek said theres a direct correlation between infrastructure and quality of life and that not allowing residents to vote on extending the sales tax is a disservice. Communications Director Sarah Prohaska read a letter from Kenneth Kroll, chairman of both the county and Port St. Lucie Sales Tax Oversight committees, who said approving the referendum in 2026 would provide certainty for long-range planning and ensure continued investment in transportation, stormwater, public safety and environmental projects.

Commissioner James Clasby opposed the 2026 ballot placement, saying he didn't want the measure competing with Amendment 3 and a School Board tax on the same ballot. Commissioner Erin Lowry agreed, saying many residents are struggling financially and may reject the measure simply because it includes the word tax. Chairwoman Jamie Fowler and Commissioner Cathy Townsend argued the county would have two opportunities if the measure were placed on the 2026 ballot. Townsend moved to keep the referendum on the 2026 ballot, but the motion failed 2-2. Clasby's motion to delay it until 2028 also failed 2-2.

Deputy County Administrator Mayte Santamaria reminded commissioners they had already approved an ordinance in March scheduling the referendum for November 2026. Keeping that date requires no action, while delaying it until 2028 would require rescinding the ordinance and adopting a new one. If voters approve the referendum in 2028 instead of 2026, it would be treated as a new infrastructure sales tax rather than a continuation.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie cuts property tax rate for 11th consecutive year
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved a property tax rate of 4.8750 for fiscal year 2026-27, down from 4.9750 in the current year, continuing an 11-year streak of annual millage reductions.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved a property tax millage rate of 4.8750 for fiscal year 2026-27 at the annual Summer Workshop held July 22-23, a decrease from 4.9750 in fiscal year 2025-26. The budget will be adopted by City Council in September, with public hearings taking place Sept. 3 and Sept. 17. The fiscal year 2026-27 budget goes into effect Oct. 1.

Since 2016, the City has reduced its millage rate by 25 percent, saving the average homeowner nearly $2,000 over a 10-year period. Port St. Lucie has the third lowest municipal tax rate out of Florida's 20 largest cities. The property tax reduction maintains Port St. Lucie's record of steadily reducing its millage rate while managing historic population growth, investing in essential infrastructure and improving public safety.

Residents can learn more about the City's budget, millage rate history and financial planning at CityofPSL.com/budget.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County sees highest home price increase on Treasure Coast, up 2.3% to $399,000
cards.teaser: Single-family home prices are rising across the Treasure Coast after drops from 2023 to 2025. St. Lucie County is seeing the highest increase in the region.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County is seeing the highest increase in the region, up 2.3% since June 2025 with a median sale price of $399,000. Martin County median home sale prices are up 1.1% since 2025, sitting at $655,000. Indian River County has seen an increase of 1.8%, with a median sales price of $400,000.

 Kelley Decowski, an award-winning realtor at REMAX in Stuart, said the increases are being driven by low supply and high demand. Decowski said buyers should start making decisions now because there are no signs that the prices are going to come back down. Decowski said inventory is low on the Treasure Coast, though the market is currently balanced for both buyers and sellers.

 Prices have dropped for condos and townhomes in Martin and St. Lucie counties and increased by less than a percent in Indian River County.

cards.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue faces $16.5M loss, 116 job cuts if property tax reform passes
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Rescue could lose $16.5 million if voters approve property tax reform in November, according to public records. County commissioners are set to discuss what thos
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue could lose $16.5 million if voters approve property tax reform in November, according to public records. County commissioners are set to discuss what those changes could mean for the fire department in a commission meeting Tuesday. The proposed reform would increase the homestead exemption over two years, and the department is bracing for the impact.

 Rick Sterl, president of the Martin County Firefighters Association, IAFF Local 2959, said most of the department's funding comes from ad-valorem and general fund revenue. If voters approve the reform, Martin County Fire Rescue's presentation outlines two stark options: cut services or cut staff. Cutting services would mean closing fire stations, ending hazmat, dive and technical rescue operations, grounding the critical care helicopter, and using firefighting equipment past its lifespan. Cutting staff would mean eliminating 116 firefighters over two years, roughly one in three firefighters in the department.

 Sterl said the consequences of either path would be felt by the public. "Any reductions is going to possibly change the outcome of the level of care the response time," said Sterl. "At the end of the day, any cuts is someone is going to pay the price." According to public records, both options create compounding problems.

 Cut services and remaining personnel can't respond properly, or cut firefighters and there won't be enough staff to maintain existing services. Fire rescue argues no version of the proposal allows the department to remain whole.

 Residents in Martin County offered mixed reactions to the potential cuts. Joe Vessichio said he doesn't believe the cuts will happen. "Neither one is going to happen, we have more than enough money," said Vessichio.

 "And even if it does, big deal, so a couple of people lose their job, they get retrained to do something else." Lisa Freitas, owner of Lisa Gay Fashions, expressed concern about what cuts could mean for public safety. "Wow, what a job they do. You can't go that route for our safety. They protect our families," said Freitas.

cards.headline: Martin and St. Lucie counties report five confirmed cases of cyclosporiasiasis
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health has confirmed 94 cases of cyclosporiasiasis statewide, including two in St. Lucie County, two in Palm Beach County and one in Martin County.
cards.body:
Growing outbreaks linked to bacteria and parasites on produce continue making headlines. The Florida Department of Health has confirmed 94 cases of cyclosporiasis statewide, including two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County.

 Ryan Boylston of Delray Beach has responded by growing his own produce in his front yard. His property includes spinach, lettuce, arugula, star fruit, bananas, peppers, pineapple and herbs that his family eats every day. Boylston started growing his own food about three years ago after struggling to find produce he felt was healthy and free of chemicals or contaminants.

 He now helps others install gardens in their own yards through his company, Urban Abundance. The other half of his property is filled with herbs and vegetables growing in raised planters similar to the ones he builds for customers. For beginners interested in starting their own garden, Boylston recommends growing crops that can handle Florida's summer heat, including spinach, sweet potatoes and yardlong beans.

 He says lettuce and tomatoes do much better during the winter months. Boylston recommends raised garden beds with smooth sides that iguanas cannot easily climb, and suggests building cages or enclosures around plants growing directly in the ground for protection.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce mother leaves nursing career as childcare costs consume 20% of household income
cards.teaser: Siedah White estimated childcare for her four children ranged from $275 per week for toddlers to $300 per week for infants, forcing her to become a full-time mom.
cards.body:
Siedah White of Fort Pierce left her job as a certified nurse assistant after childcare costs for her four children consumed approximately 20 percent of her household income. She was one of over 100 people to comment on WPTV's Facebook page about the rising cost of childcare in Florida. White said she was paying $300 per week for each infant and $275 per week for toddlers, expenses that forced her to become a full-time mom. She now hosts a video Mom blog on Instagram and TikTok.

 "I was just working just to pay childcare, and we weren't able to meet our family goals as far as needing to move into a larger place and upgrading our family vehicle," White told WPTV. The decision to leave her career came after she realized that working was not helping her family achieve their financial objectives despite bringing in additional income.

 According to the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, childcare prices increased 29 percent from 2020 to 2024, outpacing the 22 percent rise in overall prices during the same period. Childcare costs now frequently exceed the 7 percent of income affordability benchmark established by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. The Atlanta Fed examined childcare costs in Georgia and Florida and found that 85.4 percent of Florida families are estimated to spend more than 7 percent of their income on childcare.

 The study found that the estimated weekly costs for care of infant and toddler children in Florida are $268 and $208 for preschool-aged children. The median percentage of income families would need to pay for childcare in Florida is 13.9 percent, nearly double the federal affordability benchmark. The research indicates these costs are putting significant financial pressure on parents and forcing difficult decisions about work hours and employment. Some parents, like White, are choosing to leave the workforce entirely rather than continue paying childcare expenses that consume a substantial portion of their earnings.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.teaser: Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton.
cards.body:
Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized.

 The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

 Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab. With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district was able to add these on.

 The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie police find suspect hiding on roof after 80 mph chase
hero.teaser: A suspected drunk driver fled Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph before abandoning his car and running, with one suspect later found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving. Instead of pulling over, the driver accelerated to nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone on Southwest Becker Road. Police said the driver and passenger weaved in and out of traffic, ignored traffic signs and signals, then abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot.

A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home. The suspects were identified as Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46. Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie opens $28.8 million police training facility
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie cut the ribbon on a 54,283-square-foot, state-of-the-art police training center on July 24 after four years of construction.
cards.body:
The three-story facility on the Port St. Lucie City Hall grounds includes a 20-lane indoor firearms range, a tactical shoot house with configurable rooms for scenario-based training, a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for immersive decision-making exercises and a defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology. The facility also includes three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division, including 19 offices and 86 workstations.

Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin said the project ensures officers have the space, training and resources needed to continue serving the community at the highest level. Officer Brittany McNally said officers previously traveled to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training. By bringing much of that training in-house, the facility will reduce recurring costs while allowing the department to train more efficiently and effectively. The facility was designed by ADG Architecture and constructed by HJ High. Police personnel immediately began making the move into the new facility after the ribbon-cutting ceremony.

cards.headline: Indian River County Fire Rescue mourns death of firefighter Geoffrey Lang
cards.teaser: Indian River County Fire Rescue is mourning the loss of Firefighter and Paramedic Geoffrey Lang, who died while off duty Saturday night.
cards.body:
The department announced Lang's passing in a statement, calling it a regretful loss and asking the community to keep his loved ones in their thoughts. Indian River County Fire Rescue said additional information will be released in the coming days.

The Sebastian Police Department said it was joining Indian River County Fire Rescue in mourning Lang's death and wrote that his bravery and service will always be remembered. The Vero Beach Police Department also shared its condolences, saying it stands alongside Indian River County Fire Rescue during the difficult time. The department said it honors Lang's service and the impact he made on the community.

cards.headline: 3 arrested in death of 3-month-old in St. Lucie County from dehydration and malnutrition
cards.teaser: Three people were arrested Friday, nearly a year after a 3-month-old child died in St. Lucie County. Nicole Maxwell, 27, the child's mother, Robert Maxwell, 61, the child's grandfa
cards.body:
Three people were arrested Friday, nearly a year after a 3-month-old child died in St. Lucie County. Nicole Maxwell, 27, the child's mother, Robert Maxwell, 61, the child's grandfather, and Vikki Koon, 38, Robert Maxwell's girlfriend, face charges in the case according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

 Deputies, detectives and crime scene investigators responded to Lawnwood Regional Medical Center on Aug. 20, 2025, after the 3-month-old was brought to the emergency room by the child's grandparents. The sheriff's office said medical personnel notified them that the child had been pronounced deceased and exhibited injuries and conditions consistent with possible neglect. The Medical Examiner determined the child's manner of death to be homicide, with the cause of death attributed to dehydration and malnutrition.

 Each suspect faces charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse. Bond was set at $1.5 million for each defendant.

 Sheriff Richard Del Toro said in a statement that the death of a child is a tragedy that affects the entire community. He commended Detective Corporal Jennifer Diaz for her leadership and thanked the detectives, crime scene investigators, professional support staff, the Medical Examiner's Office and the State Attorneys whose commitment and teamwork led to the arrests.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police release body camera video of officer striking suspect during arrest
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police released body camera video showing an officer striking a man in an incident that started when officers responded to a reported assault of a woman under the South Bridge on Tuesday.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police released body camera video showing the moments leading up to an officer striking a man in an incident that has been circulating online. Officials said the incident started when officers responded to a reported assault of a woman under the South Bridge on Tuesday at 11:47 a.m. According to the department, officers stepped in to stop the attack, but the suspect, Justin Ikeler, 42, refused commands and raised his fists at them.

 The department said an officer then struck Ikeler to protect himself and make the arrest. Police said in a statement that when officers attempted to take Ikeler into custody, he pulled away, refused repeated commands and assumed a fighting stance with his fists raised toward the officers. Based on Ikeler's actions, the officer perceived an imminent threat of assault and delivered defensive strikes to protect himself and gain control of Ikeler so the arrest could be completed.

 Ikeler is now in the St. Lucie County Jail. The department said the investigation remains active and its release of the video is intended to provide additional context regarding the incident.

cards.headline: Community gathers to honor 9-year-old boy killed in dirt bike crash with FedEx truck in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: Family members, friends and neighbors gathered Tuesday evening to honor the life of a 9-year-old boy killed in a crash involving a dirt bike and a FedEx box tru.
cards.body:
Family members, friends and neighbors gathered Tuesday evening to honor the life of a 9-year-old boy killed in a crash involving a dirt bike and a FedEx box truck in St. Lucie County. The vigil was held less than 24 hours after the crash on East Midway Road, where the child was pronounced dead Monday afternoon. According to the Florida Highway Patrol, the crash happened around 3:07 p.m. Monday in the 600 block of East Midway Road near Fort Pierce.

 Investigators said the 9-year-old and a 12-year-old were riding a dirt bike when it collided with a FedEx box truck. The 9-year-old died at the scene. The 12-year-old was taken to a local hospital in stable condition.

 Although the Florida Highway Patrol has not publicly released the victim's identity, loved ones came together to remember the young boy with candles, balloons and prayers. Neighbors said the area is a common place for children and others to ride bicycles and dirt bikes. The Florida Highway Patrol continues to investigate what led to the collision.

cards.body:
Single-family home prices are rising across the Treasure Coast after drops from 2023 to 2025. Martin County median home sale prices are up 1.1% since 2025, sitting at $655,000. St. Lucie County is seeing the highest increase in the region, up 2.3% since June 2025 with a median sale price of $399,000. Indian River County has seen an increase of 1.8%, with a median sales price of $400,000.

 Kelley Decowski, an award-winning realtor at REMAX in Stuart, said the increases are being driven by low supply and high demand. Decowski said buyers should start making decisions now because there are no signs that the prices are going to come back down. Inventory is low on the Treasure Coast, though the market is currently balanced for both buyers and sellers.

 Cara Collins, who bought her Martin County home before the COVID-19 pandemic when prices were significantly lower, said she has no plans to sell. Collins said current prices are higher than she would hope for, and that the market has changed what would be possible for her family today. She said she would not be able to be a stay-at-home mom and be able to afford a home for her kids if buying now.

 Condos and townhomes show different trends. Prices have dropped in Martin and St. Lucie counties and only increased by less than a percent in Indian River County. Decowski said buyers need to come in pre-approved before they go looking at homes, and sellers need to price their homes realistically and present a well-maintained product.

cards.headline: Private racetrack resort community breaks ground in St. Lucie County on 650 acres
cards.teaser: P1 Motor Club is under construction on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road in St. Lucie County, replacing fairways with racing circuits and preparing to welcome its first drivers this fa
cards.body:
P1 Motor Club is under construction on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road in St. Lucie County, replacing fairways with racing circuits and preparing to welcome its first drivers this fall. The private racetrack resort community features 10 miles of racing circuits designed for street cars, race cars and go-karts. Chris DuPlessis, Director of Fun for P1 Motor Club, compared the concept to a high-end golf resort, except with a racetrack instead of a golf course.

 The first track under construction is the 3-mile Treasure Coast Track, set to open in October. Over the next six months, crews will continue work on additional circuits, including the flagship 4.5-mile P1 International Circuit. DuPlessis said the club is designed for drivers of all ages and skill levels, with kids as young as 8 years old driving go-karts all the way up to grandparents still driving their cars on track, making it a family club.

 Membership comes with a $192,000 initiation fee and $12,000 in yearly dues. The club already has 260 members. Construction on a clubhouse and homes for up to 125 residents is scheduled to begin in 2027. The development will also include condos and customizable garages with living spaces situated directly along the tracks.

 Despite the scale of the project, developers say they want to preserve the character of the region by planting trees, creating lakes, and incorporating natural landscaping throughout the property. DuPlessis said it will feel like the racetrack has been there for 100 years, comparing the scope of work to building a city. P1 Motor Club is expected to be fully completed by 2028.

cards.headline: Survey finds 64% say inflation made basics harder to afford, 42% skipped medical care
cards.teaser: A 2026 survey from eHealth found 64% of those polled say inflation has made it harder to afford basics like food, housing and clothing, with 42% saying they skipped or delayed medical care in the past year.
cards.body:
A 2026 survey from eHealth found 64% of those polled say inflation has made it harder to afford basics like food, housing and clothing, forcing many Americans to make difficult choices between necessities like rent, groceries and healthcare. The study reveals that healthcare is often losing out when people are forced to prioritize their spending.

 Medicare recipients are especially finding it challenging to afford healthcare amid rising costs. Judith Waseka, who attended a Let's Hear It community event in Vero Beach, said even with supplemental help, she and her husband are having a hard time affording their prescription drugs. "You either eat or you pay for your medication, or you sell your house or you pay for your medication," Waseka said.

 The financial pressures are leading to serious consequences for people's health. Forty-two percent of those polled say they've skipped or delayed medical care in the past year because of inflation, according to the eHealth study. This means nearly half of respondents are going without needed medical attention due to cost concerns.

 The survey highlights how inflation is forcing Americans to make impossible choices between basic necessities. When stretched budgets cannot cover housing, food and medical care simultaneously, many are choosing to forgo healthcare rather than go without shelter or meals. The findings underscore the growing financial strain facing families, particularly those on Medicare who are living on fixed incomes while trying to manage healthcare expenses that continue to rise.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks community support as husband battles head and neck cancer
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound couple is asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis, holding onto faith every step of the way.
cards.body:
Dave and Faren Motz met in South Florida before moving to Maui, where they married and raised their family. Faren raised all three of their kids and home schooled. The couple started a business and had a farm where they served children.

 Years later, they moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer. As the couple searched for the right healthcare in Florida, AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource.

 Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up, costing the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket. Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid.

 Dave, a former firefighter, had long been the family's provider. Now, Faren has stepped up to support them both, driving him back and forth from Orlando for treatment. Doctors told Dave he has an 85% chance of recovery.

 Faren works at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show their support can stop by and visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: Some Villa Del Sol residents return home nearly 2 years after structural damage forced evacuation
cards.teaser: Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County told WPTV they are able to return home after nearly two years of being displaced from their condos following structural damage found in August 2024.
cards.body:
Residents told WPTV they were notified last month they could return to their condos, after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. Katie Johnson was the first to share to WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return.

 WPTV also obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie Johnson described the work still underway at the property, saying they're still moving the dirt back under the buildings.

 Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot. Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia.

 Eric Johnson said the financial toll has been severe, explaining the family had to drain out all their savings accounts and all their 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. Katie Johnson said she is thinking of neighbors like Eric Johnson who cannot return, saying she feels so bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September, citing low demand
cards.teaser: JetBlue is ending its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport on Sept. 9, just nine months after the route launched in December.
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. Dambeck said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates, with air carriers fluctuating based off of demand.

 Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if the airline had stayed with it. Ahern said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat because it is easy and close. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

 Dambeck said JetBlue will evaluate continuously, so just because the route is gone now does not mean it will never come back. The Boston route from Vero Beach is seeing great demand, Dambeck said.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named FSL Pitcher of the Week
hero.teaser: The 22-year-old left-hander struck out 12 batters over seven scoreless innings in two appearances against Fort Myers.
hero.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for July 20-26, Minor League Baseball announced Monday.

Ware made two appearances against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels at Clover Park, starting Tuesday and returning for a relief outing Sunday. The left-hander combined to throw seven scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two walks while striking out 12 batters.

The Mets won both games in which Ware appeared. He earned the victory Sunday after pitching four scoreless innings, allowing one hit and one walk and recording a career-high eight strikeouts as St. Lucie rallied for an 11-8 win.

Ware, 22, was selected by the New York Mets in the 15th round of the 2025 MLB Draft out of LSU. He made his professional debut with St. Lucie in April and has remained with the team throughout the season.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Museum of Art opens new Jill Nathanson exhibition
cards.teaser: More than 20 works by artist Jill Nathanson are now on display at the Vero Beach Museum of Art in an exhibition running through February.
cards.body:
The Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases exhibition opened July 25 at Vero Beach Museum of Art, 3001 Riverside Drive, Vero Beach. The show features more than 20 works by the artist and runs through February.

Admission is free to members, veterans and active duty military personnel with valid identification. Non-member adults pay $12, seniors 65 and older pay $11, and students with identification pay $5.

The museum is also showing James Prosek: At Work in Holmes Gallery through October 25, consisting of projects that define the artist's first 30 years of artmaking. Another exhibition, American Made, runs through August 16 in Holmes and Titelman Galleries, featuring more than 80 works by artists including Benjamin West, Sarah Miriam Peale, Edward Moran, John Singer Sargent, Mary Cassatt, Robert Henri and Charles Alston.

cards.headline: Mets erase 5-0 deficit to beat Mighty Mussels 11-8
cards.teaser: Jeremy Rodriguez went 4-for-4, and Conner Ware struck out a career-high eight as St. Lucie scored eight runs in the second inning.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets erased an early five-run deficit with an eight-run second inning and rallied for an 11-8 win over the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Sunday afternoon at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers won the seven-game series 4-3 and finished the season series with an 8-4 advantage.

 The Mighty Mussels scored three runs in the first inning and two more in the second to build a 5-0 lead. St. Lucie responded with eight runs in the bottom of the second and moved ahead for good.

 Randy Guzman delivered the decisive hit, lining a two-out, two-run single that turned a 5-4 deficit into a 6-5 Mets lead. Julio Zayas followed with a two-run single to extend the advantage to 8-5.

 The Mets added three runs in the third. Elian Peña hit an RBI single, Jacob Reimer drove in a run with a double and Trey Snyder added a sacrifice fly to make it 11-5.

 Conner Ware took over on the mound in the third inning and settled the game down for St. Lucie. Ware pitched four scoreless innings, allowed one hit and one walk, and struck out a career-high eight batters. He struck out the side swinging in the fourth and struck out the side looking in the sixth before earning the win.

 Fort Myers scored three runs in the seventh against Luis Sotillo, who was making his Mets debut. Sotillo recovered by retiring six of the final seven batters he faced and carried the game through the eighth inning.

 Elwis Mijares worked a perfect ninth on six pitches to record his third save.

 Jeremy Rodriguez led the Mets at the plate, going 4-for-4 with a double, an RBI and two runs scored from the No. 9 spot in the order. Zayas and Peña collected two hits apiece.

 Reimer, beginning a minor league rehabilitation assignment for a groin injury, went 1-for-3 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and two runs scored. He played all nine innings at third base.

 The Mets improved to 11-18 in the second half and 44-51 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game road series against the Dunedin Blue Jays on Tuesday. First pitch at TD Ballpark is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Fall Short in 15-14 Loss to Fort Myers
cards.teaser: Randy Guzman hit two home runs and drove in six as the St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run deficit in a 15-14 loss to Fort Myers.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run first-inning deficit but fell one run short in a 15-14 loss to the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Saturday night at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers scored eight runs in the opening inning and survived several St. Lucie rallies to earn its third consecutive victory.

 Mets starter Ethan Lanthier was charged with seven runs on five hits and two walks before being removed with two outs in the first inning. Harry Genth delivered a three-run double during the Mussels' early outburst.

 Mets Answer With Five-Run First Inning

 St. Lucie immediately responded with five runs against Fort Myers starter Matt Barr in the bottom of the first. Antonio Jimenez, Branny De Oleo and Simon Juan each recorded RBI hits to cut the deficit to 8-5.

 The Mighty Mussels added three runs against Franyel Diaz in the third inning. Ramiro Dominguez drove in two with a single, and Byron Chourio hit a solo home run to extend the Fort Myers lead to 11-5.

 Trey Snyder helped St. Lucie pull closer in the fourth inning with an unconventional trip around the bases. Snyder's ground-ball single was mishandled by shortstop Quetin Young, who then committed a throwing error that allowed Snyder to score and another run to cross the plate.

 The play cut the Mussels' lead to 11-7.

 Guzman Homers Twice

 Randy Guzman hit a two-run homer against Ramiro Villanueva in the fifth inning to bring the Mets within two runs.

 Villanueva later hit consecutive batters and was ejected. St. Lucie loaded the bases with one out, but reliever Adam Falinski retired Elian Pena on a popout and Snyder on a groundout to preserve the 11-9 Fort Myers advantage.

 Young answered with a three-run home run over the batter's eye in the sixth, pushing the Mussels' lead to 14-9.

 Guzman responded again in the bottom half of the inning, launching a three-run homer to make it 14-12.

 He finished the game 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, six RBIs and two runs scored.

 Ninth-Inning Rally Falls One Run Short

 Ricardo Paez opened the ninth inning with a solo home run that gave Fort Myers a 15-13 lead and provided what proved to be a crucial insurance run.

 Francisco Toledo scored on a wild pitch and throwing error with one out in the bottom of the ninth. Marco Vargas then homered to right field with two outs, pulling St. Lucie within one run at 15-14.

 Brent Francisco struck out Chase Meggers to end the game and record his third save.

 Michael Hilker Jr. earned the win after pitching 2 1/3 scoreless innings of relief for Fort Myers. Lanthier took the loss.

 Jimenez went 2-for-3 with two walks and three runs scored. Vargas, De Oleo and Juan added two hits apiece.

 The Mets fell to 10-18 in the second half and 43-51 overall. The Mighty Mussels improved to 14-14 in the second half and 51-42 overall.

 The teams will conclude their series Sunday at Clover Park. First pitch is scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

cards.headline: Zayas Homers Twice as St. Lucie Mets Cruise Past Mighty Mussels
cards.teaser:
Julio Zayas homered twice and Trey Snyder continued his hot stretch at the plate as the St. Lucie Mets defeated the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels 8-2 Tuesday night at Clover Park.

The
cards.body:
Julio Zayas homered twice and Trey Snyder continued his hot stretch at the plate as the St. Lucie Mets defeated the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels 8-2 Tuesday night at Clover Park.

The victory in the series opener was St. Lucie's fifth win in its last six games.

The Mets held a 1-0 lead through two innings before breaking the game open with four runs against Fort Myers starter Eric Hammond in the third.

Randy Guzman drew a bases-loaded walk to bring home the first run of the inning. Snyder followed with a two-run double before scoring on a throwing error after Antonio Jimenez singled, extending the Mets' lead to 5-0.

Jimenez added a sacrifice fly in the fifth inning to make it 6-0.

Zayas provided the rest of St. Lucie's offense with solo home runs in the sixth and eighth innings. He became the second Mets player this season to record a multi-homer game, joining Guzman.

Zayas finished 3-for-4 with his fifth and sixth home runs of the season.

Snyder also went 3-for-3 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and a run scored. He has collected seven hits over his last two games.

St. Lucie starter Conner Ware pitched three scoreless innings, allowing no runs while striking out four.

Emilio Obispo earned the win after allowing two runs on two hits over four innings. He walked three and struck out three.

Zack Mack pitched a scoreless eighth inning before Elwis Mijares worked the ninth and induced a 4-6-3 double play to end the game.

The Mets improved to 9-14 in the second half and 42-47 overall. The Mighty Mussels fell to 10-13 in the second half and 47-41 overall.

The teams will play the second game of the series Wednesday at Clover Park. The Mets will hold their annual Summer Camp Day, with first pitch scheduled for 11:10 a.m.

cards.headline: Messi bathed Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot, now they meet in World Cup final
cards.teaser: A 2007 charity calendar photo shoot paired teenage Lionel Messi with infant Lamine Yamal. Now 19 years later, they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, took the photos after Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró near Barcelona who wanted to participate.

 Soccer destiny paired her baby boy with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

 Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed with Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation.

 The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's final. Monfort, 58, is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. He said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win.

cards.headline: President Trump to Attend World Cup Final in New Jersey with Stepped-Up Security
cards.teaser: The World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey has been designated a Level 1 Special Event with President Trump attending the trophy presentation and enhanced security from multiple federal agencies.
cards.body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup began with 48 teams playing over 39 days. Now it comes down to one final match Sunday in New Jersey. As Argentina and Spain prepare to take the pitch, a sprawling network of federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies continue with a game plan two years in the making to ensure the final is safe.

 A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament.

 The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

 The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle.

hero.headline: Big Taste of Martin County returns to Stuart in October to support youth mentoring programs
hero.body:
Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties is preparing for the return of Big Taste of Martin County, a food and spirits event scheduled for Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart. The annual fundraiser brings together local restaurants, chefs and community partners to support mentoring programs for children across the Treasure Coast.

Guests can sample food, wine and beer from area businesses while participating restaurants compete for Big Taste awards and local bragging rights. Spritz Stuart plans to feature several menu items during the event, including a Tuscan salmon dish, a smash burger and a specialty cocktail called the Fig & Flame.

According to Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties, the event helps fund mentorship opportunities for children who are currently waiting to be matched with a mentor, known as a Big. The nonprofit serves children and families throughout Palm Beach and Martin counties through one-on-one mentoring relationships designed to support academic achievement, confidence and personal growth.

Community members can support the mission by purchasing tickets, attending the event or volunteering to become a mentor. More information about the event and mentorship opportunities is available through Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties.

cards.headline: Recycled fishing line becomes friendship bracelets at Vero Beach Museum of Art
cards.teaser: Coastal Connections and the Vero Beach Museum of Art will transform discarded fishing line into friendship bracelets during a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. Aug. 8.
cards.body:
Discarded fishing line will find new purpose as friendship bracelets when art and marine conservation come together at the Vero Beach Museum of Art. The museum and Coastal Connections will team up for a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. Aug. 8, with hands-on activities, gallery tours and lessons about protecting local marine life.

Coastal Connections will lead a hands-on activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium, where visitors can make friendship bracelets using recycled fishing line collected from local waterways. Participants also can learn about the organizations Fishing Line Recycling Program. The museum has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp.

Kendra Bergman, founder and executive director of Coastal Connections, said the partnership with the museum is a great example of how the organization is working with the community to introduce everyone to marine conservation and environmental protection in unique ways. Second Saturday includes free museum admission throughout the day. Coastal Connections was founded in 2017 with a mission of advancing the survival of sea turtles by educating and connecting people to the environment.

cards.teaser: A Christmas in July vendor market will take place Saturday at 2001 SW Murphy Rd in Palm City starting at 10 a.m., featuring food trucks, an ornament decorating station and vendors.
cards.body:
A Christmas in July vendor market will bring holiday cheer to Palm City on Saturday starting at 10 a.m. The event takes place at 2001 SW Murphy Rd. The market will feature food trucks, an ornament decorating station, vendors and more.

The Christmas in July event is one of several activities happening on the Treasure Coast and in Palm Beach County this weekend. Other events include the Boynton Beach Night Market on Saturday at 5 p.m. at Centennial Park and Amphitheater, and Rock'n Riverwalk on Sunday at 1 p.m. on St. Lucie Avenue in Stuart.

cards.headline: Rockn Riverwalk free concert series continues Sunday on Stuart waterfront
cards.teaser: The Downtown Business Association of Stuart is inviting the public to enjoy Rockn Riverwalk, a free open-air concert series held every Sunday at 1 p.m. on the Riverwalk Stage on St. Lucie Avenue.
cards.body:
The Downtown Business Association of Stuart is inviting the public to enjoy Rockn Riverwalk, a free open-air concert series held every Sunday on the Riverwalk Stage. The concerts take place at 1 p.m. on the waterfront at St. Lucie Avenue in Stuart, offering live music in an outdoor setting.

The weekly series provides residents and visitors with a regular opportunity to enjoy live music along the Stuart waterfront. The events are free and open to the public, continuing the tradition of bringing community members together for outdoor entertainment on Sundays.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Recreation Department presents 52nd Aerial Antics Youth Circus at St. Edwards School
cards.teaser: Vero Beach Recreation Department will present 2016 Takeover, the 52nd Aerial Antics Youth Circus, at St. Edwards School from July 30 through Aug. 1.
